correctness.rationale: Direct local equations yield an invariant order-three base and one-step hub dependence. Exact kernel calculation gives im A as the even-parity hyperplane, and a characteristic-two cancellation proves A^6=I on this subspace. Solving the 1-, 2-, and 3-step fixed-space conditions gives dimensions p+epsilon_p, 2p, p+2q+epsilon_p+2epsilon_q and 2p+4q; Möbius inversion yields orbit counts and the union-of-two-proper-subspaces argument gives the six-cycle criterion. Degenerate p=0 or q=0 cases are explicitly included and checked. 827208 direct trajectory checks and 168 separate exact matrix calculations corroborate these identities; finite checks do not replace the universal proof. Because the odd-order graph has kernel generated by the all-ones vector and the periodic image is an invariant hyperplane, each periodic point has one periodic predecessor and one nonperiodic predecessor, proving the exact 2d basin formula.

value.rationale: Triangle/pentagon flowers are a natural first mixed-length subclass of XOR flower networks from the historical asynchronous literature. The theorem identifies an exact one-step entrance law and all primitive orbit counts for all p,q, together with a non-obvious sharp motif threshold: a triangle plus a pentagon lacks period six, while two pentagons or one pentagon with two triangles support it. It distinguishes synchronous from asynchronous behavior, and addresses natural dynamical invariants rather than an arbitrary enumerative slice. The exact uniform attraction-basin law, with one transient feeder per recurrent point, upgrades a recurrence count to a full dynamical basin classification.
